Create ONE finished cinematic vertical 9:16 narrative keyframe for the Nasa–Paeces film El Trueno, ideally 864x1536. No sheet, collage, border, lettering, title, captions, watermark or logo. Use the supplied images only for their stated continuity roles, never copy their sheet layout. Same world as the approved Nasa triptych: immersive Colombian highland CUT-PAPER scenery, matte broad flat faces, internal cut edges, folded rock, overlapping planes at three distances, physical occlusion and cast shadows. Figures have simplified almost-flat paper faces, not rounded clay dolls, CGI or photographic skin. Water, clouds and mist are flat cut-paper shapes too, never cotton or smoke. Frame extends edge to edge, no display base, table, studio or diorama box. Preserve precise age, clothing, hat, material and scale of the reference identities. Do not import objects, people or actions from preceding shots unless specifically listed below. No pan-Indigenous costumes, copied sacred patterns, gold, crowns, feathers, magical beams or invented ritual. Selected narrative: Martín Kuskue's first El Trueno account via Bernal 1953; the elder appearance is a declared editorial convention retained from the approved triptych, not claimed as wording of this version.

SHOT b3b — El retiro
DAYLIGHT fading to blue-gray dusk. ONE elderly Trueno seen from behind walking away along a narrow dry ridge toward a SMALL highland lagoon far ahead. The cape edge has the same broad paper rhythm as cloud layers without physically becoming a cloud. Foreground ochre path enters lower left and leads to figure then lagoon; close dark paper cliffs at either side and far mist strata.
